summary: Charlene Elizabeth Makley specializes in Tibetology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (~1991–1999) under Norma Diamond, Luis Oscar Gómez, Bruce Mannheim, Jennifer Robertson, and Roy Rappaport, later becoming an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College (~2000).
Charles A. Moore was a philosopher who studied at Yale University (~1926–1932). He served as a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1936–1967) and edited Philosophy East and West (~1951–1967).

Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (~1991–1996) under Paul Groner and became Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America (~1996).

Charles D. Orzech works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1977–1986), chaired the Religious Studies Department at UNC Greensboro (~1984–2013), and was a Fellow at the National Humanities Center (2009–2010).

Charles Duroiselle worked in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Associated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1907), he taught at the University of Yangon (~1920–1930) and was Superintendent for the Archaeological Survey of India and the Department of Archaeology (1919–1931).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied at Kingswood College (until ~1925) and served as a Senior Lecturer at the University of London (~1953–1959).

Charles Elliott worked in Indology after studying at Fort William College (~1801–1804). He served with the East India Company (~1795–1830) and later as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1836–1856).
Charles Gabriel Seligman was an Indologist and scholar who studied at St Thomas' Hospital (~1892–1896). He held a post at the University of London (~1910–1934).

Charles Goodman specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (~1996–2002) under Allan Gibbard, Luis Oscar Gómez, Thomas Hofweber, and Philip J. Ivanhoe, becoming Associate Professor at Binghamton University (~2003).

Charles H. Long was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1950–1962). He held posts at Chicago (~1956–1974), UNC Chapel Hill (~1974–1987), Syracuse University (~1987–1990), and UC Santa Barbara (~1990–1996).

Charles Hallisey works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1981–1988), he held posts at Amherst, Loyola University Chicago, the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2005–2006), and Harvard University (~2007).

Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1856–1860). He served as Fellow and Tutor there (1860–1864), Chair of History at Presidency University, Kolkata (1865–1892), and Librarian at the India Office (1893–1903).

Charles Malamoud is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Paris, he held posts at the University of Lyon and as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1998).

Charles Philip Brown was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at Haileybury and Imperial Service College (~1814–1817), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and as Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1879).

Charles Ramble works in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Durham University and under Michael Aris (~1980–1985), he held posts at Tribhuvan University, Wolfson College, Oxford (~2000–2009), the University of Oxford (2003), and the EPHE (~2009).

Charles Rieu studied at Geneva and Bonn under Humbert, Freytag, Gildemeister, and Lassen. A scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he was Curator at the British Museum (1847) and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge (~1894–1902).

Charles Rockwell Lanman was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney and under Rudolf von Roth. He taught at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and served as Professor at Harvard University from 1880.

Charles S. Prebish is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Case Western Reserve, studying under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He held positions at Penn State (~1972–2007), Calgary, Toronto, and Utah State (~2007–2011).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969), later holding a post at Ohio University (~1969–1972).

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and a founding member of the Asiatic Society (1784). He served as librarian for the East India Company (~1770–1836), the India Office Library and Records (~1801–1836), and East India Company College (~1806–1836).
